hook.text: Your AI says ninety days. The policy says thirty.
hook.promise: Follow one policy passage through retrieval, augmentation, generation and evidence checking.

design.visualThesis: An amber policy passage is the visual thread from document to retrieved evidence to a cited answer; missing evidence leads to an explicit stop.
design.motionGrammar: Stable amber evidence moves through the pipeline; query and document merge into a prompt; missing evidence takes a stop branch. Motion uses scene-local seconds and measured voice cues.
design.assetLanguage: Original SVG document fragments, source links and diagrams; fictional log-retention example marked on screen.

scenes.narration: How long do we keep logs? An AI might say ninety days. But our example policy says thirty. That gap is where RAG can help.

motion.action: Cross out the unsupported 90-day answer and reveal the policy fragment with 30 days.

scenes.purpose: Passages indexed for search; embeddings are one option.
scenes.narration: First, prepare the documents. Split them into passages and index them for search. Embeddings are one way to match meaning.

motion.action: One document separates into three passages; the retention passage stays amber and joins a search index.
motion.settle: Passages indexed for search; embeddings are one option.

scenes.purpose: Relevant passage plus source metadata, not yet an answer.
scenes.narration: Now ask the question. Retrieve the relevant policy passage. The search result is evidence for the model, not the final answer.

motion.action: The question searches three passages and selects the retention excerpt with its source ID.
motion.settle: Relevant passage plus source metadata, not yet an answer.

scenes.purpose: Answer and source passage connected by the same reference.
scenes.narration: Put the question and that passage into the prompt. The model writes an answer: thirty days, with a link back to the source.

motion.action: Question and policy fragment move together into a prompt, then a cited 30-day answer appears.
motion.settle: Answer and source passage connected by the same reference.

scenes.purpose: No unsupported exception invented; stop and say evidence is missing.
scenes.narration: That does not guarantee truth. Search can miss, documents can be outdated, and models can misread them. Missing evidence should trigger a clear refusal.

motion.action: A question about exceptions takes a no-evidence branch to an explicit insufficient-evidence answer.
motion.settle: No unsupported exception invented; stop and say evidence is missing.

scenes.purpose: A citation must support the answer; maintain the searchable index.
scenes.narration: RAG means retrieval augmented generation. Retrieve, then answer with evidence. Keep the index current, and check whether the answer really matches its source.

motion.action: Trace the amber passage through search and generation, then link answer back to its source for checking.
motion.settle: A citation must support the answer; maintain the searchable index.

outro.takeaway: Retrieval supplies evidence; generation still needs checking.
outro.cta: Keep the index current and check each answer against its source.

revision.reason: User explicitly requested remake; editorial and production decisions delegated.
revision.example: Fictional operations policy retains application logs for 30 days; not a real retention recommendation.
